input.reasoning: The candidate asserts that realistic semiclassical-to-memory-burdened transitions are smooth over a finite interval rather than instantaneous; the existing node bb218573 asserts the transition is practically instantaneous, so Hawking emission ceases almost immediately once the effect takes over. These are direct contraries: the same considerations (how the memory-burden parameter turns on, over what interval in entropy or evaporation time) bear on both, and they cannot both hold. Per §2, a claim and its denial are one node hosting the debate, so this is a match with the source recorded as denying the node as canonically stated. Search evidence: I searched four framings, including two negation framings ("transitions happen instantaneously rather than smoothly"; "the effect switches on abruptly with no smooth transition window"); the instantaneity node was the top hit under both negation framings (0.81, 0.715) and also scored highest under the candidate's own exact wording (0.768). No node states the smooth-transition proposition affirmatively: the only continuity-adjacent hits are conditional cosmological claims (65f3b122, a236aad5) whose substance is BBN bounds and dark-matter fractions, not the character of the transition itself. Residual uncertainty: the candidate's "realistic" qualifier and the node's bundled consequence clause are superficial differences; neither changes which evidence bears on the disputed core, so they do not defeat the match.
input.relationship_notes: bb218573 is the direct counterpart (negation/contrary) of the candidate: instantaneity against smoothness over a finite interval. 65f3b122 and a236aad5 are conditional downstream claims (BBN bounds, dark-matter fraction caps) that take a continuous crossover as a premise; the candidate is a premise of theirs, not the same claim. cd14d3da is a related but distinct threshold claim about where semiclassical evaporation is blocked (half the entropy plus order one percent), not about how fast the transition unfolds. 351acde4 (the burdened phase halts evaporation) and 960a19bf (microscopic black holes evaporate essentially instantly under semiclassical physics) are adjacent but separate propositions. Note for the Steward: the canonical form of bb218573 bundles a consequence ("so Hawking emission ceases almost immediately once the effect takes over"); that trailing inference belongs in an argument's written form rather than the canonical text, and the wording may be tightened to the disputed core (e.g., the transition's timescale) without changing the node's identity. A later rewording in the smooth direction would flip recorded stances and should be done only with that flip handled.
